clue.text: Soldier hired a waistcoat

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
to let a house is to hire it out, so let can mean hired

explanation.surface: A soldier has rented a waistcoat for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless jacket or bodywarmer, a kind of waistcoat.

clue.text: Girl, only half seen, grabbing a blue blouse

indicators.note: grabbing says the half-word holds the other letters inside it
only half seen means just the first half of the word girl is shown

parts.note: blue means risque or bawdy, as does ribald

explanation.surface: A girl, partly glimpsed, snatches a blue blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour for the blouse, but it means risqué. 'only half seen' takes the first two of Girl's four letters, and 'grabbing' wraps them round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi was a loose red shirt-style blouse, modelled on those worn by Garibaldi's followers.

clue.text: Bald guy crushed American beetle

indicators.note: crushed means squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bald man has squashed an insect from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges BALD GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladybug is the American name for the spotted beetle the British call a ladybird.

clue.text: Old woman of ill repute has run into Jethro

indicators.note: into says one letter is placed inside the surname

parts.note: Jethro Tull was an 18th-century English agriculturist (and a rock band)
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A disreputable woman bumps into a man named Jethro.
explanation.walkthrough: Jethro Tull, the farming pioneer or the band, gives TULL.
explanation.definitionFit: Trull is an archaic word for a prostitute.

clue.text: Having dreadfully bad hole in, like some boots

indicators.note: dreadfully says the preceding words are badly treated, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something dreadfully worn has a hole in it, as old boots do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges the letters of BAD HOLE IN; 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy boots were studded with hobnails on the sole for grip and wear.

clue.text: Crewman's around at front of boat, in addition to boater

indicators.note: around says the crewman's letters surround the others

parts.note: a hand is a crew member, and the apostrophe s stands for is

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the word boat

explanation.surface: A sailor goes round the bow of a boat, and wears a straw hat too.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat straw hat, so the definition is the band added to it. 'around' wraps the crewman round the rest; 'front of' takes B from boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatband is a ribbon fitted around a hat such as a straw boater, an extra on it.

clue.text: In bedroom, suffering tedium

indicators.note: suffering means damaged or in a bad way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stuck in a bedroom, someone is bored stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges BEDROOM; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom is the weariness of having nothing interesting to do, the same as tedium.

clue.text: It upped and left; in some distant past

indicators.note: in says the letters before it go inside the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any'

indicators.note: upped in a down clue says the letters climb, that is read from the bottom

parts.note: to quit is to leave, so left can be quit

explanation.surface: Something got up and walked out, back in the far-off past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' looks like 'got up', but in a down clue it reverses the word It. 'in' then puts the pieces inside the word for 'some'; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiquity means ancient times, the far-off past.

clue.text: Mild Bolshevik, without energy, beginning to tire

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says Lenin's letters go around the next one

parts.note: Lenin led the Bolsheviks
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word tire

explanation.surface: A moderate revolutionary, lacking energy, starts to flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: E goes inside LENIN. 'beginning to' gives T from tire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means gentle or tolerant in judgement, not harsh.

clue.text: Indulged Duke's' high social standing

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
rank is status or a high position in society

explanation.surface: A duke enjoyed his elevated place in society.
explanation.definitionFit: To have drunk is to have indulged in alcohol.

clue.text: Set rudder at sea, as standard on vessel

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Instructions to fix a boat's rudder, as is normal practice on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like 'usual', but here it is a flag. 'at sea' rearranges SET RUDDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign, nicknamed the red duster, is the flag flown by British merchant ships.

clue.text: Island kingdom's transport

definitions.meaning: a Polynesian kingdom of islands in the South Pacific
a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India

explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island monarchy, and a tonga is also an Indian horse carriage.

clue.text: A fry-up? Sounds like it

parts.note: a dish of fried leftovers whose name imitates the noises it makes in the pan

explanation.walkthrough: The dish is a British favourite of leftover potato and cabbage fried together.
explanation.definitionFit: This British dish of fried leftover cabbage and potato is named for the sizzling sounds it makes while cooking.

clue.text: Pull girl back — she's dropped behind

indicators.note: back says the pull and girl words are both read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to drag something is to pull it
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone tugs a girl back because she has fallen behind the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses both pieces together as one run, so the girl ends up first. The definition is a person, the one who has dropped behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a person who lags, a straggler who has fallen behind the rest.

clue.text: Maxi-coat I restyled — that's obvious to anyone

indicators.note: restyled means remade in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion remake of a long coat is plainly evident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restyled' rearranges MAXICOAT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Axiomatic means self-evident, accepted as true without proof.

clue.text: Man returned gun to water

indicators.note: returned says the letters for Man are written backwards

parts.note: IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man
the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A man brought a gun back so he could water something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, IOM, which 'returned' turns into MOI.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something is to wet it slightly, as you would water a plant.

clue.text: Monkey in school turned over stationery

indicators.note: turned over says the whole assembly is read backwards, upwards in this down clue
in says the monkey goes inside the school

parts.note: Repton is an English public school in Derbyshire
an ape is a primate, loosely called a monkey

explanation.surface: A monkey in a classroom flips over some writing supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Repton is an English public school in Derbyshire. With the monkey inside, the whole thing reads REPAPETON, and 'turned over' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepaper is writing paper, a staple of stationery.

clue.text: I shall leave behind feelings of animosity

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I shall
to will something is to leave it behind in a testament

explanation.surface: Someone vows to go away, leaving resentment in their wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or malice felt towards someone.

clue.text: Man left on time, taking a short way

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A man left punctually, taking a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'taking' are link words placing the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard is a man's first name.

clue.text: The delicacy of a quadrille partner

definitions.meaning: a shellfish prized as a luxury food
the creature that dances in the Mock Turtle's quadrille in Lewis Carroll's Alice

explanation.definitionFit: Lobster is a luxury seafood, and in Alice in Wonderland the Lobster Quadrille is a dance with lobsters as partners.

clue.text: Recompense prepared for any eventuality involving unknown people

indicators.note: involving says one set of letters wraps around the others

parts.note: an answer off pat is ready for anything that comes up
Y is a mathematical unknown
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: Compensation set aside for every eventuality, covering people not yet known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' as in 'off pat' means rehearsed, ready for anything; 'involving' wraps it round the unknown and the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Recompense is money given as reward or compensation, a payment.

clue.text: Sought reward, holding upper class daughter

indicators.note: holding says the reward word contains the next letter

parts.note: a purse is a prize of money
U denotes upper class

explanation.surface: A society daughter chased a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class is a known convention, as in 'U and non-U'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pursued something is to have chased or tried to get it.

clue.text: Former soldiers need help with setting up introductions

parts.note: ex means former
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: setting up in a down clue says the letters are raised, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Veterans need assistance with arranging some opening speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' turns AID into DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Exordia, plural of exordium, are the opening parts of speeches or treatises.

clue.text: Flowers to plant and reach maturity? Not with Virginia Woolf & Co.

parts.note: blooms are flowers
to plant something is to bury it in the ground

indicators.note: not with means the letter W, the abbreviation for with, is left out

parts.note: to grow up is to reach adulthood

explanation.surface: A gardening question about flowers maturing, suddenly turning to a famous novelist and friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not with' removes W (short for 'with') from GROW UP, giving GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf was a leading member of this circle of early 20th-century writers and artists who met in a London district.

clue.text: Colonel used to cover camera

definitions.meaning: a soundproof housing placed over a film camera

explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp was David Low's cartoon diehard, and a blimp is also a soundproof casing for a film camera.

clue.text: Stares in wonder at disease of birds

definitions.meaning: a poultry disease caused by gapeworm

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gawps open-mouthed gapes, and the gapes is a disease making fowl gasp.

clue.text: I sleep a short time — it's not appropriate

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone admits napping for a moment is unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or out of place for the occasion.

clue.text: Contrived with valuable card to take trick. East going out of turn

parts.note: a trump is a card of the suit that beats all others

indicators.note: going out of turn says the letter moves from its proper place in the word to another position

parts.note: to dupe is to trick someone

explanation.surface: A bridge player wins a trick with a trump, while East leads out of turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out of turn' moves the E in DUPE from the end to the front, making EDUP. 'take' links TRUMP to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is one fabricated or falsely made up, i.e. invented.

clue.text: Page editor and I put right, having removed corn etc.

parts.note: to cure is to put right or heal

explanation.surface: A page editor and the writer fix a problem with corn and similar items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corn' looks like a crop; it is the hard skin on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicure treats the feet, removing calluses and corns, so the feet have been treated.

clue.text: Leading player's taken about one step

indicators.note: taken about says the star wraps around the other letter

parts.note: a star is the lead performer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The lead actor has taken a single step.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step in a staircase.
